title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on model selection, version pinning strategy, and fallback/rollback plans after running latency and quality benchmarks. Redwood reviewed benchmark results, recommended pinning to a quantized v2.1 for latency-sensitive routes and a higher-quality v2.3 for long-form summarization, and discussed canary rollouts plus automatic fallback to hosted variants. Action items: share benchmark sheet, security doc, and confirm final pinned versions by next week.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share updated benchmark spreadsheet and per-route cost calc (due 2025-05-14)
Liam O'Connor: Draft model pinning recommendation doc with rollback steps (due 2025-05-16)
Priya Patel: Provide final list of production routes to pin and latency SLOs (due 2025-05-16)
Maya Chen: Share security SOC2/ISO summary and runbook link (due 2025-05-13)
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet and security deck
Customer to confirm two routes for initial pinning and target SLOs
Schedule on-prem/private demo for Veridian infra team (tentative May 20)
Redwood SE to propose canary rollout plan and automatic fallback thresholds
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Noah Patel (Redwood); Priya Patel, Carlos Mendes, Aisha Rahman, Ben Lowe (Veridian)
Links shared: benchmark_spreadsheet.xlsx (drive link), security_deck.pdf (link), runbook-private-deploy.md (link)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week's benchmarks, confirm model versions to pin, discuss rollback and fallback behavior and plan next steps.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): all right everyone thanks for hopping on, I think we have about 40 minutes, do a quick status and then dive into the benchmarks and model pinning recommendation
00:18 Priya (Veridian): sounds good, thanks Maya, yeah we ran the test harness yday across our three main routes, jak and long form, and short prompt summarization, so curious to hear your take
00:35 Liam (Redwood): cool, i'll give the high level then show the sheet, so we ran v2.1 quantized, v2.3 float, and the hosted small variant for fallback, basically latency, cost, and rouge/qa style metrics
00:50 Carlos (Veridian): quick note our latency target for user-facing chat is 200ms p95, background summarization can be up to 1.2s p95
01:05 Noah (Redwood): thanks for that, that is helpful for route-level pinning
01:20 Priya: ok let's see the numbers
01:25 Liam: (shares spreadsheet) so for chat route v2.1-q gave ~170ms p95 on our dedicated-like nodes with 4g KV cache, cost/unit is about 0.6x of v2.3, quality delta on rouge is -3 points but user-level QA we saw minimal regressions for short replies
01:48 Aisha (Veridian): there were a couple of hallucination cases in v2.1-q on product names, is that expected with quantization?
02:05 Liam: yeah quantization can slightly change tokenization edge cases and logits leading to rare errors, but we can mitigate with prompting and reranking, or pin the higher quality v2.3 for the sensitive routes
02:30 Ben (Veridian): what's the hosted fallback look like when dedicated capacity is saturated? we want automatic failover not to break sessions
02:45 Maya: we recommend an automatic routing policy: primary = pinned dedicated model, fallback = hosted variant with same architecture but lower cost, plus a canary for new pins; we can preserve context by streaming the KV cache where possible, otherwise session resumes are OK
03:05 Carlos: any security differences between hosted fallback and private? we have EHR data, so retention and KMS are big concerns
03:20 Maya: noted, for health data we recommend Private control plane + KMS, but hosted fallback can be configured to never receive PII by striping user identifiers client-side; we'll share the security deck with exact controls
03:38 Priya: circling back to model rollback, what does an automated rollback look like? say we pin v2.1-q and then see a quality regression on the test set
04:00 Liam: good question, our recommended approach: 1) canary roll for 5% traffic and monitor the eval set metrics and production signals, 2) if delta exceeds thresholds (we're suggesting >5% quality drop or >20% error increase), auto-rollback to previous pinned version and reroute traffic to hosted variant until investigation
04:28 Priya: thresholds seem reasonable, can we tune thresholds per route?
04:35 Liam: yes per-route thresholds; the console supports route-level alerts and automatic policy overrides
04:48 Aisha: what's the operational overhead for pinning many routes? we have 12 routes across product
05:00 Maya: you can group routes into policies, and we can automate rollouts via canaries and schedules; typical setup is pin the top 2-3 latency-sensitive routes first, then expand
05:18 Ben: any concerns around model catalogs being updated unexpectedly? we want consistent behavior during the POC
05:30 Noah: catalogs are versioned, but cloud-hosted catalogs may add new model variants; pinning is explicit — we will set the team’s account to not auto-upgrade pinned models
05:45 Priya: good. show us the specific recommended pins
05:50 Liam: ok, per the sheet: Route A (user chat) -> pin v2.1-quant (model id rwd-v2.1-q-2025) for latency; Route B (long summary) -> pin v2.3-flt (rwd-v2.3-float-2025) for quality; Route C (search rerank) -> use v2.2-mid as primary and hosted small variant as fallback
06:20 Carlos: that v2.1 ID looks like a generated id, are those stable across deploys?
06:28 Liam: yes model ids are immutable per build; versions like v2.1-q will map to a specific artifact hash and can be pinned indefinitely until you change it
06:40 Priya: what about quantized artifacts, are they reproducible if we want to run on-prem?
06:50 Liam: we can provide the quantized artifacts for private deployment and include the quantization config; in on-prem case you control the exact binary so it's reproducible
07:05 Priya: perfect
07:12 Aisha: any observed regressions in the test suite we should be worried about?
07:20 Liam: only a handful — mainly rare entity failures in v2.1-q for long-tail product names; we ran 10k prompts, failures <0.2% but showed up in autosampler; recommend adding a lightweight reranker on the sensitive route
07:40 Priya: reranker — is that part of the Redwood offering or custom?
07:48 Noah: we have a built-in reranking hook and you can add a custom filter; it's supported in the console as a step in the route pipeline
08:05 Ben: cost impact if we add reranking?
08:10 Liam: small increase depending on rerank size; typically +10-30% per call but reduces downstream error costs; sheet has per-route estimated uplift
08:25 Priya: ok next, can we talk about canary rollout schedule and monitoring signals?
08:30 Maya: suggested plan: 1-day internal canary (5-10%) with synthetic traffic and production shadow for 24 hours, 7-day gradual increase to 50% for user traffic, observe p95 latency, error, and eval-set quality metrics. Rollback triggers are threshold breaches or human abort
09:00 Carlos: what constitutes a human abort? who gets notified?
09:08 Maya: notification to the oncall list and the POC stakeholders; we can add Slack hooks — we'll set up paging for the SRE if p95 jumps >2x
09:22 Priya: ok on the monitoring we want token-level cost and latency breakdowns, can we see that per-route?
09:30 Liam: yes token-level breakdown and per-model breakdown is in the console; we'll share screenshots but it's live once you onboarded to the account
09:40 Aisha: reminder we are experimenting with batching to reduce cost, how does batching interact with pinning?
09:48 Noah: batching is runtime-level and can apply across pinned models; if a pinned model supports larger batch sizes it will be used, otherwise the runtime falls back to smaller batch which can affect latency distribution. We suggest tuning batch windows per route
10:05 Priya: any gotchas for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) when using pinned quantized models?
10:15 Liam: main ones: you need matching CUDA/cuDNN drivers and the same kernel selection; quantized kernels sometimes require additional libs. We'll provide a runbook for infra to validate. Also consistent compiler/runtime matters for exact reproducibility
10:35 Carlos: we'll need that runbook, pls share
10:40 Maya: will do, it's linked in the notes
10:45 Priya: security question — with hosted fallback, is data ever stored in the hosted variant logs? we need no PII retention in hosted fallback
10:55 Maya: by default hosted has retention, but we can configure no-persist mode and ensure payloads are obfuscated; for strict compliance we recommend private-only for certain routes and hosted fallback only for non-PII hashed metadata
11:15 Ben: any SLA differences between dedicated and hosted fallbacks?
11:22 Maya: yes dedicated reserved capacity has SLA guarantees; hosted is best-effort with region-level availability; we can include this in the contractual addendum for Dedicated purchases
11:35 Priya: let's talk about a rollback example — say we detect hallucination spike after pushing v2.1-q to 100%
11:45 Liam: the system will compare running eval metrics vs baseline; if spike > configured threshold it triggers the policy to rollback to previous pinned version and optionally route to the hosted safe variant. We'll also send an automated incident ticket to the team
12:10 Carlos: how fast is an automatic rollback typically executed?
12:18 Liam: within seconds of the policy trigger — the policy engine flips routing at the ingress level. There's also a cool-down period to avoid flapping
12:35 Priya: do we have examples where auto-rollback misfired?
12:42 Noah: rare, usually due to misconfigured thresholds or noisy signals; we recommend conservative thresholds during initial rollout
12:55 Aisha: operationally who owns adding a new pinned version? our product team or infra team?
13:04 Maya: ownership model is flexible — product can request a pin, infra can approve. We can set RBAC so only a defined group can change pins; we'll show role examples
13:20 Priya: show us the RBAC UI
13:28 Liam: (screen share) here — you can add a pin, attach canary policy, set thresholds, and add fallback. I'm toggling into the pin history — see audit log entries with user and timestamp
13:45 Priya: audit logs are good; we need export to our SIEM as well
13:52 Liam: we support syslog/forwarding and S3 export for audit logs
14:05 Ben: any limitations with model catalog compatibility across on-prem and hosted? for ex model A is optimized for Triton and another for the Redwood runtime, will that cause mismatches on fallback?
14:20 Noah: the runtime maps compatible variants; if the architecture differs we provide a compatible hosted variant with same API contract. In rare cases we suggest a shim or conversion step and we'll coordinate with your infra team
14:45 Priya: let's finalize the list of two routes to pin this week
14:50 Priya: Route A (chat) and Route B (summary) are the candidates
14:55 Maya: confirm Route A -> v2.1-q and Route B -> v2.3-float as recommended in the sheet; we'll add the canary at 5% and a 24-hour synthetic run
15:10 Priya: agreed, we'll confirm by Friday EOD
15:20 Carlos: about cost modeling, can we get per-1M token cost with pins?
15:30 Maya: yes the sheet includes per-route cost assumptions; I'll annotate the cell with dedicated vs hosted unit costs
15:42 Priya: awesome, a few micro items — can we get a short runbook for rollback and a simple test script to simulate a hallucination spike?
15:55 Liam: yes we'll provide a test harness example and a playbook for rollback steps
16:10 Maya: recap of next steps: Ramirez send benchmark & security, Liam send pinning doc & harness, Priya confirm routes and SLOs, schedule private demo if infra wants it. any other items?
16:30 Ben: nope that covers it thanks
16:35 Maya: thanks everyone we'll follow up with the sheet and security deck
16:40 Priya: thanks all

Notes end.
